clue.text: The ultimate in non-celebrity?

parts.note: the most complete lack of fame is to be a person nobody has ever heard of

explanation.surface: A wry question about the most extreme form of obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a playful description: someone of no celebrity whatsoever is simply not known to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Total absence of celebrity means being a person of whom nobody is aware, the clue's teasing paraphrase.

clue.text: An Ulster deployment, initially starting out impartial

indicators.note: a deployment is an arrangement of forces, signalling the letters are reordered
out means the chosen letter is dropped from Ulster
initially picks the first letter of starting

explanation.surface: A neutral peacekeeping force posted to Northern Ireland at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S of 'starting' from ULSTER, giving ULTER, then rearrange with AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking no side in a conflict, like a non-aligned country, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Island republic some guru annually turns up in

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher visits an island nation once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny Pacific island state, one of the smallest sovereign countries in the world.

clue.text: Small boy finally asked what could be long and dirty

definitions.text: what could be long and dirty

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
Ken is a boy's name

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of asked

explanation.surface: A little lad finally poses a cheeky question.
explanation.walkthrough: A long one includes a bank holiday; a dirty one is a romantic getaway, British idioms.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saturday-and-Sunday break can be long or, slangily, a dirty one spent with a lover.

clue.text: Fighter is some giant, in more ways than one

definitions.meaning: a fighter is a member of an army

definitions.text: some giant, in more ways than one
definitions.meaning: each part of the word giant, GI (an American serviceman) and ANT (the warrior caste of ant), is an army man of sorts

explanation.surface: A fighter described as a giant, impressive on several counts.
explanation.walkthrough: Split giant into GI and ANT: a GI is a US serviceman, and a soldier ant is a fighting ant, so each part of the giant is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in an army is a trooper, the plain synonym; the second half is the cryptic split.

clue.text: Protest movement raised firm support at start of year

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: CO is company, a firm
a cup supports, as in a bra cup

indicators.note: at start of picks the first letter of year

explanation.surface: A protest group, its firm support raised at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The Occupy movement camped out in financial districts from 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2011 anti-capitalist campaign that set up camps in city financial districts, a protest named by a verb.

clue.text: Run away with turncoat 5

parts.note: to desert is to run away from duty
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Fleeing, alongside a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to the answer at 5 across. Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Britain's 7th Armoured Division of World War II was an army man nicknamed this.

clue.text: Deviant tendency of drunk, heading off to drink another can

indicators.note: to drink means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: merry is a mild word for drunk

indicators.note: another suggests a different version of can, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker heads off to down another can, a deviant habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like part of the drinker's story, but 'to drink' signals one piece swallowing the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency to stray from what is right or true, the noun from erring.

clue.text: Went climbing with Ben before journalist comes round

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: comes round says the journalist encloses the next word

parts.note: ED is an editor, a journalist
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Hiking with a friend called Ben before a reporter turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' reads as a companion but is a Scottish peak.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale peaks as a sport is the verb behind alpinist activity, so went up hills.

clue.text: Archbishop weds two intimate solvers near the 17 23

indicators.note: two in front of the phrase asks for its letters to be written twice over

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you, and you the solvers are addressed in Paris, home of the Arc de Triomphe

explanation.surface: A churchman marries two close friends of the crossword fans near a Paris landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Tu is the intimate (familiar) French form of 'you', the solvers; 'near the 17 23' says the language is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Tutu was the Anglican Archbishop of Cape Town, the best-known holder of that title.

clue.text: Gym users taking oxygen for energy are arguably a dispiriting lot

indicators.note: taking signals that one letter is brought into the word as a swap
for marks what is given up in exchange for the newly taken letter

parts.note: people using a gym are working out, so they are exercisers
E is the physics symbol for energy
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: People at the gym, short of breath, might be thought a depressing crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of the gym users is replaced by O. 'Dispiriting' is the pun: those who cast out evil spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who drive out demons literally remove spirits, so they dis-spirit, a punning reading of the definition.

clue.text: See 24
Nurse returned after putting in quiet hour working in kidney units

indicators.note: after putting in tells us the turned nurse has other letters placed inside it
returned means the nurse's letters are read backwards

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A nurse back at work after quiet time in a renal ward.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the microscopic filtering structures of which each kidney contains about a million.

clue.text: Uniform colour of foreign boulevard, one taken for university

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and altered, signalling a rearrangement
taken for means one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The colour scheme of a uniform on a boulevard abroad, with a university swap.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the U of BOULEVARD with I to get BOILEVARD, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This dull greenish-brown shade is the classic colour of military uniforms.

clue.text: Pre-DVD CD programme divides round number by a hundred

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the next piece
to programme is to arrange, signalling the letters are reordered

parts.note: O is zero, a number
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A television programme on an old disc format, with numbers being divided.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled DIVIDES becomes VIDEDIS, which goes round O; C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Before DVDs, optical discs like LaserDisc stored films, a compact disc holding moving pictures.

clue.text: Revealing pictures of 1 5s and other 1s

parts.note: the answer to 1 across is unknown, and X is the classic unknown in algebra
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of army men
Y is another algebraic unknown, here made plural

explanation.surface: Scans showing anonymous troops and other nameless figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references: 1 is UNKNOWN and 5 is SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiographs reveal the inside of the body, so they are pictures that expose what is hidden.

clue.text: Monument to head crimper arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's tribute to a top stylist being set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crimper' is slang for a hairdresser, which makes the surface about a salon.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Parisian arch is a monument to French military victories, housing the tomb of an unidentified fighter.

clue.text: 5s repeatedly sad, messed up studies again

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the army piece is written twice

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of army men

indicators.note: messed up means the letters of sad are jumbled

explanation.surface: Troops, sad and in a mess, keep going over their books.
explanation.definitionFit: To look through a text once more is to go over it a second time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One may have a blowout meal after day out on the underground

indicators.note: out says the letter for day is removed from the meal

parts.note: dinner is a main meal
the Tube is the London Underground railway

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a big feast after a day out on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowout' looks like a slap-up meal but is a burst tyre. The Tube is London's underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable ring inside a tyre is what bursts in a puncture, so it can suffer a blowout.

clue.text: Girl group going on for ever?

definitions.meaning: a British all-female pop act of the 1990s

explanation.surface: A girl band whose career seems to last indefinitely.
explanation.walkthrough: Eternal was a British female vocal group of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without end is everlasting, and the name of a 1990s British vocal group.

clue.text: Fish found in case of brass ornaments

indicators.note: found in tells us the fish sits inside the other letters
case of means the outside letters, the shell of the word

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fish discovered inside a box of brass decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: These rigid bracelets are decorative pieces of jewellery worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Highest point I somersaulted in a gym

indicators.note: in places the turned self inside the gym

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym lessons at school

indicators.note: somersaulted means flipped over, so the self is read backwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A gymnast's best moment: somersaulting in a gym.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest point of an orbit from Earth, extended to mean a peak or climax.

clue.text: See 17
Deserted child found by extremely 1 5 after note translated

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged
extremely picks the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: 1 across is unknown
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An abandoned child found next to an anonymous war grave, after a note is translated.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' is here the number, V, not the cross-reference to 5 across. The French phrase means a foundling.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a found child: a foundling, an infant abandoned by its parents and later discovered.

clue.text: Send rude online message to lover

definitions.meaning: to post an abusive message on the internet

explanation.surface: Firing off an insulting message online to one's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet slang for an abusive post, and a romantic partner, as in an old sweetheart.

clue.text: Pigment from 17 23 location, featuring in advertisement

parts.note: the Arc de Triomphe stands in Paris
the French word vert, meaning green, is tucked inside advertisement

explanation.surface: A paint colour sourced from a famous Paris landmark, starring in an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect step: 'advertisement' contains VERT, which is French for the colour wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: This poisonous copper arsenite was once a bright emerald pigment and insecticide.

clue.text: Return of the French Lieutenant's first 1 5 supporter

indicators.note: return of means the French article is read backwards

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the officer's rank

parts.note: 1 across is unknown, and Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Recalls the novel The French Lieutenant's Woman, with a soldier's backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 5 is the cross-reference to the fighter of 5 across, unlike its use in 24.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation or comrade fighting alongside an army man is its partner in war.

clue.text: Mentally prepares to pronounce name of Dickensian murderer

indicators.note: to pronounce asks for the word as heard rather than as written

parts.note: Bill Sikes is the brutal killer of Nancy in Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: Someone gearing up to say the name of a Dickens villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting oneself ready mentally, as in gearing up before a contest, is a common verb sense.

clue.text: Like a colour that is reflected in a red glow

indicators.note: in places the turned abbreviation inside the glow

parts.note: a blush is a reddening of the face

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: IE is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A colour that is reflected in a reddish light.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a red shade, but the answer is the opposite end of the spectrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinged with the shade of the sky, resembling that colour without being fully it.
